decisions.reason: As a core extension of the firm's established airfield lighting and control know-how, this product fits its strongest knowledge base and can be improved through in-house R&D and installed-base learning.

The surveillance display is closely related to the firm's integrated airport operations business, so management is likely to keep it while refining it through customer feedback and system-integration capabilities.

A broad airport systems training program complements the firm's installed solutions and service model, making it useful for absorbing operational knowledge from customers and supporting the wider portfolio.

This narrower training course is the easiest to fold into other services, but because it still builds directly on the firm's airfield ground lighting expertise it is more likely to be retained than withdrawn.

Airport collaboration software strongly matches the firm's move toward integrated, data-driven and collaborative operations, and its existing domain knowledge gives it good capacity to improve and commercialise the tool.

The multilateration surveillance system is technologically adjacent to the firm's airport guidance and control activities, and with internal R&D in a growing industry management would likely keep investing rather than exit.
